Let

\[
S=\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\sum_{m=1}^{100}2^{-\lfloor 101k/m\rfloor}.
\]

For each positive integer \(n\), let \(A_n\) be the number of pairs \((k,m)\) with \(1\le m\le 100\) and

\[
\left\lfloor \frac{101k}{m}\right\rfloor=n.
\]

Then

\[
S=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}A_n2^{-n}.
\]

For fixed \(n,m\), the condition is

\[
n\le \frac{101k}{m}<n+1
\iff
mn\le 101k<m(n+1).
\]

Since \(m<101\), this interval has length less than \(101\), so it contains at most one multiple of \(101\).

Let \(s\) be the residue of \(mn\) modulo \(101\).

- If \(s=0\), then \(mn\) itself is a multiple of \(101\), so it works. This happens for all \(m\) exactly when \(101\mid n\), giving \(A_n=100\).
- If \(s>0\), the next multiple after \(mn\) is \(mn+101-s\). It lies in the interval iff
  \[
  mn+101-s<mn+m \iff s+m>101.
  \]

Now count \(A_n\) modulo \(101\):

- If \(n\equiv 0\pmod{101}\), then \(A_n=100\).
- If \(n\equiv 100\pmod{101}\), then \(s=101-m\), so \(s+m=101\), and no \(m\) works. Thus \(A_n=0\).
- If \(n\equiv 1,2,\dots,99\pmod{101}\), pair \(m\) with \(101-m\). The residues are complementary, and exactly one of the two conditions \(s+m>101\) holds. Hence each pair contributes exactly one, so
  \[
  A_n=50.
  \]

Thus the sequence \((A_n)\) is periodic with period \(101\), and

\[
A_1=\cdots=A_{99}=50,\qquad A_{100}=0,\qquad A_{101}=100.
\]

Therefore

\[
S=\frac{50\sum_{n=1}^{99}2^{-n}+100\cdot 2^{-101}}{1-2^{-101}}.
\]

Since \(\sum_{n=1}^{99}2^{-n}=1-2^{-99}\),

\[
\begin{aligned}
S
&=\frac{50(1-2^{-99})+100\cdot 2^{-101}}{1-2^{-101}}\\
&=\frac{50-100\cdot 2^{-101}}{1-2^{-101}}\\
&=\frac{50(1-2^{-100})}{1-2^{-101}}\\
&=\frac{100(2^{100}-1)}{2^{101}-1}.
\end{aligned}
\]

\[
\boxed{\frac{100(2^{100}-1)}{2^{101}-1}}
\]
